name: Chemical Data Science & Automation
tagline: Data pipelines, lab automation, and informatics-driven experiment design.
seo_title: Chemical Data Science & Automation — paper summaries, news & innovations | Chemisters
seo_description: Follow Chemisters Chemical Data Science & Automation on LinkedIn and Facebook: paper summaries, news and innovations in chemical data, lab automation, design of experiments and reproducibility.

definition.lead: Chemical data science turns the data chemistry produces, from instruments, experiments and the literature, into reliable knowledge, and automates the pipelines that handle it.
definition.body: Clean, well-described data is the fuel of every model and every automated lab. This field covers data capture, standards, electronic lab notebooks, analysis pipelines and statistics, so that results are findable and reproducible.

timeline.title: The Design of Experiments
timeline.text: Ronald Fisher publishes his book on planning experiments statistically.
timeline.why: Randomization and factorial design entered science.

timeline.title: Response surfaces
timeline.text: George Box and K. B. Wilson introduce response surface methodology.

timeline.title: The CAS Registry
timeline.text: Chemical Abstracts Service starts assigning registry numbers to substances.
timeline.why: A unique identifier for every substance.

timeline.title: PubChem
timeline.text: A free public database of chemical structures and assay results is launched.

timeline.title: InChI
timeline.text: IUPAC releases a standard identifier for chemical structures.

timeline.title: ChEMBL
timeline.text: An open database of bioactivity data is launched.
timeline.why: Fuel for machine learning in drug discovery.

timeline.title: The FAIR principles
timeline.text: Guidelines for findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable data are published.
timeline.why: Adopted by funders and journals worldwide.

timeline.title: The Open Reaction Database
timeline.text: An open, structured database for chemical reaction data is introduced.
timeline.why: Aims to fix the shortage of shareable reaction data.

quiz.q: What does FAIR stand for in data management?
options: Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable
Fast, Accurate, Integrated, Reliable
Free, Available, Indexed, Readable
Filtered, Archived, Inspected, Reported
quiz.explain: Published in 2016 and now widely adopted.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of design of experiments?
options: It reveals interactions between factors with fewer runs than changing one factor at a time
It removes the need for any statistical analysis
It needs only a single, carefully chosen experiment
It works only in industry, not in research labs

Very large data sets that need special storage
Data that was deleted but can still be recovered
Encrypted data that only the owner can read
quiz.explain: Without it, data cannot be reused.

options: Models need negative results to learn what does not work
To fill the notebook so it looks complete
Because funding agencies pay per page
They are never useful, so this is not needed
quiz.explain: Published data is biased toward successes.

quiz.q: What should you do with an outlier?
options: Investigate it before deciding whether to exclude it
Delete it immediately to keep the data clean
Ignore it, since one point never matters
Copy it several times to strengthen the trend
quiz.explain: Some outliers are errors; some are discoveries.

quiz.q: What is a key benefit of an electronic lab notebook?
options: Searchable, structured records linked to data
It is always free
It needs no backup
It replaces experiments
quiz.explain: Paper notebooks are hard to search and share.

options: The spread of measurements
The average
The maximum
The sample size
quiz.explain: A larger standard deviation means less precise data.

quiz.q: Data leakage in machine learning means…
options: Information from the test set influences training, inflating performance
Data stolen from a lab's servers by hackers
Files lost because a hard drive failed
Data encrypted so that models cannot read it
quiz.explain: A common cause of over-optimistic results.
